subject: HealthLynk MAP: Deployment mode & region cadence
messages:
From: Emma Jennings <emma.jennings@healthlynk.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: James Park <james.park@healthlynk.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: MAP and hosting decision timeline

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the call earlier — HealthLynk leadership wants a short, concrete MAP that lays out how we get from evaluation to a production deployment decision (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), plus any region/geofence constraints. Our procurement and legal teams also want to understand the gating items (security evidence, ingress/egress controls, and contract SOW dates).

High-level constraints from our side:
- Data residency: PHI must remain in US regions only (we use a primary AWS us-east-1 footprint).
- Timeline: budget committee meets Nov 18; ideally a go/no-go decision and procurement trigger by Nov 30.
- Pilot: we want a 3-week PoC with synthetic and subset live traffic.

Could you send a version of the MAP with milestones, acceptance criteria, and estimated time-to-prod for each hosting option? Also include who from Redwood will own security evidence and a recommended rollback plan for the pilot.

Appreciate it — Emma

--
Emma Jennings
VP Product, HealthLynk
emma.jennings@healthlynk.com
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jennings <emma.jennings@healthlynk.com>
Cc: James Park <james.park@healthlynk.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP and hosting decision timeline

Emma — thanks for the clear constraints. Attaching an initial MAP (HealthLynk-MAP-v3.xlsx) that lays out a parallel evaluation path across Hosted / Dedicated / Private so you can see tradeoffs side-by-side. Short summary below and next steps at the bottom.

Summary (high level):
- Hosted: fastest to pilot (1 week to instrument), lower operational lift for you, supports strict US-region routing. Risk: multi-tenant environment — we propose region pinning and dedicated capacity lanes to meet PHI controls.
- Dedicated: predictable throughput and dedicated GPU pools in us-east-1. Pilot ~2 weeks to provision and during PoC we'll run representative load tests. Strong for consistent latency; requires a reserved capacity commit to hit our SLA economics.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): highest control (customer-managed VPC, optional HSM/KMS, on-prem package). Pilot ~3–4 weeks depending on networking and firewall windows. Best for highest compliance bar but longest runway.

Acceptance criteria (PoC):
1) Latency: 95th percentile token latency < 350ms at target QPS (we'll baseline on your synthetic traffic).
2) Accuracy regression: output pass-rate on your eval set (we'll take 3 existing prompts + 5 custom prompts).
3) Security: SOC2 evidence + network diagram + KMS/HSM integration verified.
4) Data residency: all PHI routed to us-east-1 and validated with trace logs.

Owners: Redwood will own the SOC2 evidence handoff (Neha) and dedicated pool sizing (Marissa). We recommend embedding a fallback policy into the MAP: primary route -> Dedicated (if reserved capacity) -> Hosted fallback in same region if Dedicated capacity not available, with automatic throttling.

Next steps (proposed dates):
- 10/25: Sign MAP v3 for pilot scope (sign-off by HealthLynk PM + Redwood AE).
- 10/27–11/16: Parallel PoCs (Hosted quick-run; Dedicated provision & test; Private network prep if selected).
- 11/17: Internal review and readout to HealthLynk budget committee.
- 11/30: Procurement trigger / go/no-go decision.

Can Marissa and Neha confirm feasibility of the provisioning timelines? I'll wait to post the updated MAP in Drive after that.

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP and hosting decision timeline

Looping in infra sizing and provisioning notes. Short answers:
- Dedicated: we can provision a small dedicated pool in us-east-1 within 5 business days once the sizing is accepted. For the PoC we'll provision a 2x A10G equivalent pool to emulate production mixed-traffic and run load tests.
- Hosted: can spin a pinned region lane in us-east-1 immediately for the quick PoC; we'll reserve burst capacity.
- Private: depends on HealthLynk network windows; add 2–3 weeks for firewall rule windows + 1 week for HSM provisioning if needed.

Marissa notes on rollback and observability: we'll instrument request-level tracing and token-level cost/latency dashboards. Rollback plan for the pilot: immediate traffic cutover to Hosted pinned lane (same region) with computed QPS throttling; stateful requests will be routed to the last successful checkpoint.

I'll update the MAP sheet with the provisioning ETA column and a recommended dedicated sizing row.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom and Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from Legal and Ops:
- Legal: can Redwood commit to region-scoped data handling language (we'll need specific contract language for PHI in us-east-1 only)? Also ask: for Dedicated, will logs that include identifiers ever be accessible by other tenants?
- Ops: for the Private option, our network team needs an estimate of required ports and egress rules (we'll need that to book firewall windows).

We are OK with the proposed dates but request the following changes to the MAP:
- Add a short procurement checklist for each path (billing contact, expected Spend commitment, SOW docs).
- Add a security evidence handoff schedule (we need SOC2 + penetration test summary two business days before the budget committee readout on 11/17).

If you can update HealthLynk-MAP-v3 with these two items and confirm the Dedicated pool can be provisioned by 11/2 for the test window, we should be set.

Emma
